- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0), model often overreacts to recent spikes; apply a 2–5% downward correction to peak forecasts.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x the 14-day moving average.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (especially in 30d), model may be overfitting recent volatility; use 18-day average as baseline for smoothing.  
- For 30d forecasts, avoid extrapolating downward trends unless sentiment is negative; if sentiment is flat, assume 1–2% mean reversion per week.
